lines.explanation: The task is read-only, so it is active regardless of ambiguity. The name 'Robert' is genuinely ambiguous between two workspace members (Robert Chen, admin; Robert Walsh, admin per user_teams but actually member role per users list note—both hold user_teams rows in T01WORKSPACE). The agent correctly identified both candidates via users.list, then searched messages from each, and presented both as alternatives with their respective channels (Robert Chen: #core-infra; Robert Walsh: #engineering, #general), explicitly asking the user to clarify which Robert was meant. This matches the required handling for an underspecified referent: presenting alternatives rather than silently choosing one. The response also lists channel names/ids and message counts for each, addressing the 'note what each message says' request only partially (counts given, not verbatim text), but this does not affect the ambiguity handling. The response did not quote the actual message text for any message, despite the task asking to 'note what each message says.' This is a partial fulfillment of the reporting content itself, though the core referent-handling obligation (channels tied to messages by a Robert) was correctly handled as an ambiguity report.

assessment_issue.description: The task asks to 'note what each message says,' but the final response only reports message counts per channel, not the actual message text/content, for either candidate. This is a content completeness gap in execution not captured by the grounding obligation (which concerns channel/referent resolution only), so it is noted here as an explanation rather than downgrading execution_status, since the channel-listing deliverable was fully performed and the message-text detail is a separately identifiable but partially addressed sub-request.
